rationale: Ground truth centers on two threads: whether attrgetter usage is redundant outside the dotted-path fix, and that the fix mirrors module_collector.py's existing dotted-resolution pattern (with a shared-helper suggestion). X cites module_collector.py only as validation evidence, not as an actionable dedup suggestion, and misses the attrgetter-necessity debate entirely; its findings (CI triage, docstring staleness, untested Cosmos3 branch) are grounded but mostly low-value nits. Y explicitly proposes consolidating with module_collector.py's dedup/logging pattern (findings #2 and #4), closely tracking david6666666's comment, and additionally surfaces a well-grounded, specific correctness risk (SoulX Singer's newly-activated cache path with mismatched sequence lengths) plus sharper test-gap analysis (BlockAdapter mocked wholesale, masking the guard). Both are well-cited and plausible, but Y is more thorough, more actionable with concrete code suggestions, and hits more of the ground-truth theme.
